steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Gerald, are you coming to ring the bell with me or something?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Is that weird?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: It is. I asked you once before to help me ring the bell, and you were having none of it. You ended up sending Raimund instead.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I guess that did happen.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I thought you didn't like the sound.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Can't say either way. After all these years.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: After all these years, you still haven't gotten used to it.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: You'll have to forgive me. That sound doesn't carry good memories.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Clément... do you still remember Eileen?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Eileen...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: How could I forget? If the two of you hadn't saved me back then, the bandits would've thrown me down the canyon long ago.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Haha, she was the one who insisted on saving you. I didn't want to stick my neck out.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: You're not supposed to say that to my face.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Hahaha! Sorry, sorry.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: We set up camp last night. Didn't get the greatest haul, and it wasn't easy to handle either.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Raimund bled his game while I lit the fire. I was watching that tiny flame gradually sputtered to life, and I don't know what came over me, but I suddenly started thinking of Eileen.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Gerald...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: To be honest, I hadn't thought of her for the longest time. It was only when she came to mind that I realized...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I can't even remember her face.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: She was always a bit of an outcast among us. She once told me that seeing the flowers all over the monastery and hearing the sound of the bell would set her heart at ease.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: There aren't many flowers to look at these days.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Sadly true.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Eileen loved the sound of the bell here. Up until the day she left us, when she insisted on waiting until the bell rang to close her eyes.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: So that's why you don't like it.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Maybe I'm just afraid... Afraid it'll be a harbinger of bad news.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: If only we had enough medicine back then, her injuries might not have taken a turn for the worse, and it might not have come to that...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: There are no ifs.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I hope she finds salvation.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Yes, we all do.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Gerald, is it true that you've decided to leave?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I didn't think it'd be this sudden...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I should've told you earlier, but never had a chance.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: It's probably going to be hard on Raimund and Fortuna for a while. Those kids have always gotten along. They're not going to take it easy.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Raimund's too young. He was so little when he first came here, he doesn't remember a whole lot. He doesn't yet understand what it means to be Sarkaz.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: But he will understand. He will come to terms with it.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Perhaps that is the Sarkaz's fate.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Fate isn't a pleasant word.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Hah, you have a point, but I can't find a better one.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Alright, I should go visit Eileen.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: We'll be walking different paths from here on out, so I guess this is where we part ways.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Wait... Gerald!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I, I'll go with you! It's only a slight detour, and won't get in the way of anything!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Oh right, look! The blooming season just started, so we can pick some flowers to give to Eileen!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I'll go with you...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: No, Clément. You're confused.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I'm... what?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: This isn't the path meant for you. You go up those steps over there. Keep going up, the scenery is prettier from up there.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Will you get to see that beautiful scenery?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Go ring the bell, Clément. Don't waste time. That is where you belong.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Take care, brother.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: What are you talking about, Fina? This has nothing to do with Seniora Lemuen!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Liar! Who else could fix up a patron firearm for you? Only that Lateran.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Why would you think that?!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: How can you tell if I'm lying or not? Fina, do you get how I'm feeling right now at all?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I really wish I could understand, Tuna, but I just don't get it anymore!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: The halo says you're telling the truth, and that your pain is no less than mine!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: But if that's true, how do you still have the heart to sit there baking pizzelle? How can you spend time around those Laterans like it's nothing?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I just don't get it, Tuna...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: It's because... I want everyone to live their best lives.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: We don't actually have a choice, do we? Even though Avus Stefano never said it himself, and nobody talks about it with us, I've always known, deep down in my heart.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Laterano will let us back in. I overheard them saying that our monastery is actually a very powerful building, and Laterano absolutely will want us to go back.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I also know that Patruus Gerald and the others... They, they might not be able to come with us...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: But I still want to try my best! If I can get the Laterans to understand that Gerald's people are all good, then maybe–

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Maybe what? They'd agree to let us all live together in Laterano?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I get it now... Is that why you're always so willing to chat with that Lemuen woman? You think you're putting in a good word for them?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Did you beg her? You think we have to get on our knees and beg for Raimund's people to not get left behind, is that it?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: You're trying to get them to change their minds. So what do you have to show for it?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I... I'm still working on them...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: You're wasting your time.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Wasting it on a hope and a prayer, Tuna.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: How are we different from Raimund? Or Caroline?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Raimund can do way more than I can... and Caroline is a lot smarter than me.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: See, you get it.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: They're splitting us up. They've accepted us as their people, but at the same time, they're looking down on the ones we truly belong with.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I can't accept it. I'd rather not go to Laterano at all.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: But, Fina... Didn't we agree that one day, we'd leave the wastes and go to Laterano together?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: That we'd go live in a world without hunger or cold, a world filled with flowers rather than empty barrens as far as the eye can see?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: That's just childish dreaming, Tuna.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Do you really think so? You think it's just an empty dream?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I'm not as optimistic as you are. All I know is, ever since those Laterans showed up, the air in the monastery has gotten weirder and weirder.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: It's true, our lives here have been incredibly difficult, but I've never resented that!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I love listening to Avus Stefano's sermons, and Patruus Gerald's stories about the past.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Sometimes, when we didn't have enough food, Caroline would slip us a couple extra pieces of jerky, or Amita Nina would give an extra scoop of the thickest veggie porridge to Raimund, and we'd get together and share it.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I was fine with that.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: But what about now?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Everyone always talks about how good Laterano is, but all I've ever seen of it is those people messing up our lives!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I understand you need to vent, Fina, but you can't blame Seniora Lemuen for that!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Am I venting? Okay, maybe I am.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: But, have you heard what everyone has been talking about in private? Have you noticed that Patruus Gerald and the others are coming by less and less?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: While you've been busy delivering food to Lemuen, while you've been busy making your stupid pizzelle... Do you have any idea what Caroline's people have been eating?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: You don't know anything.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: What...? Wait, Fina, what are you saying?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: What's going on with Caroline? I didn't know...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Yeah. You don't know anything at all.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: It's not your fault, it's mine. If I didn't see it with my own eyes, I never would've known how bad the situation actually is.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Tuna, if through our halos, you can feel even a fraction of what I'm feeling right now–

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Then hand your patron firearm over.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina? What are you going to do?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Just hand it over.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: There's no reason for us to pray to these things.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Give it to me!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Something's wrong with you, Fina... It's too dangerous. I, I can't give it to you!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Why not? Didn't you say you'd share it with me?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I did say that, b-but, this is different!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: You said you didn't get me at all, but I should be the one saying that... What's gotten into you, Fina? Wake up!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I'm all too awake!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I've never been so awake! You wanna talk about prayer? About the empathy only Sankta have? I've had enough!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I don't need to be special! All I want is–

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: You can't...!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina, don't be like this––!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Aaaaaaargh––!!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina...?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Urgh... Ahh! Ahhhhh!!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: All I want... is for everyone... to stay together...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina? What's wrong with you? You're scaring me...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: FINA!

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Yo. Finally caught up to you guys.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: So, what's the word? Everything going well?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Serpilia, you need to notify us in advance if you're going to act on your own.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Don't be such a hardass, will ya? All I want is to finish the job as soon as possible.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: First, the good news. I found Lemuen. She's inside the monastery.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: And then the bad news— she doesn't want to come with us.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: She always has her own agenda. Couldn't get through to her at all.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Hey, don't frown at me. Go drag her out yourself, if you've got what it takes.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Huh? Alright what...? Wait, you've gotta be joking, right?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Serpilia, let me give you a little insider tip from the Notarial Hall.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Federico never cracks jokes. He isn't capable.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I will locate her myself and ascertain her thoughts.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: What, do you think I'm lying to you or something?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I can't be certain that you're telling the whole truth.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Federico.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Now I understand why so many girls in the Curia have you blacklisted.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Well, whatever, let's set that aside for now. What's the situation over there? Did you manage to talk to the people?

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Senior Richele...?

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Is this one with you?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Yes. We're all colleagues.

steps.name: Elderly Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: What else do you want to know, young Sankta?

steps.name: Elderly Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: We have nothing here, nothing at all... We also have nothing to say. You shouldn't have come...

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Amita Nina! How could you say that? We were the ones who reached out to Laterano... You didn't have a problem with it then, did you?

steps.name: Nina
steps.text: A problem? *sigh* I should've told Stefano a long time ago not to expect anything from Laterano.

steps.name: Nina
steps.text: Yes, yes, Julian, throw them out! We never should've let the Laterans in. We don't need their help! Get them out of here now!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Umm...

steps.name: Julian
steps.text: Calm down, Amita Nina!

steps.name: Julian
steps.text: What's gotten into you? Weren't you just saying you'd go welcome our guests?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Seems like the two of you need to sort some things through in private. Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.name: Julian
steps.text: S-So sorry! Amita Nina here just got a bit worked up... Umm, I don't think we need any help, I just need to take her to get some rest. Come find me if there's anything you need to talk about later!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Uhh, yeah! Make sure she gets some rest!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: That was kind of odd.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Looks like things aren't going too well for you over here.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: What was that about?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Things seemed fine at first, but then I have no idea what happened. Hrm.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Federico, you were the one who wanted to interrogate the residents. Did you notice anything?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That woman's mood was unstable. While it's not unusual for a person to change their mind mid-conversation, it's rare for someone to forget the topic entirely and change their demeanor.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: And so you mean...?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I do have a theory.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But it's just speculation at this point. I will discuss it if the likelihood rises significantly.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Then that's that.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Besides some of the residents being kinda loopy, you must've made some other discovery?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: C'mon, Reverend Executors. Let's put our heads together.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: So putting it plainly... That bishop dumped all this extra work just for the sake of the Sarkaz living here?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Didn't we mention we were willing to bring them back to Laterano? He's leaving everyone out here to starve in the cold just for those Sarkaz? He detained a Lateran nuncio just for those Sarkaz?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Seriously? First, that traitor Andoain leaves, and now we get this merciful, compassionate bishop?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Whew. Alright. Cool.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I'm not exactly into the drama, but is he out of his mind?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: No wonder Lemuen couldn't agree with him... Considering what the Sarkaz did in Londinium, those Victorian dukes are probably furious.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: If word got out that His Holiness was cavorting with the Sarkaz now, his plans for the Summit of Nations would be through.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Sounds pretty serious.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Federico, if I remember correctly, the task given to Lemuen and Oren was to provide assistance and reclaim this monastery for Laterano, right?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: A good call, seeing as how this structure could serve as a fort and has a rather unique history. Definitely could come in handy.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Especially when the time comes for us to reach out to Iberia again.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: At least for now, there's no need for us to stoke conflict and burn bridges here.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: By the way, Federico, did you recognize that Sarkaz back there?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Who is he?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A mercenary.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: The average conversation between the two of you is about as interesting as 'What'd you eat last night?' 'Dinner.'

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Federico, how much do I have to pay you for a few extra words? You name the price, and I'll send the bill to His Holiness.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have never considered this question.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Give the guy a break. Oh, right. We know now Lemuen is well, but... what about Oren?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: The guy ran off a while ago. Even Lemuen doesn't know where he ended up.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: But he's pretty good with the self-preservation. If you ask me... he's probably hiding somewhere, planning his next move.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Huh? Uh...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: A bell? Where's that sound coming from?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The ringing of the bell signifies the beginning of the sermon.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Should we head over? There won't be anyone in the monastery during the sermon, so we could look for Oren.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No. I'll attend the sermon.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Woah, talk about out of character.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I need to ascertain the overall condition of this monastery to judge whether it can maintain stable function under current circumstances, or if outside intervention is needed.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Attending a sermon where a large number of residents will be present is a good observation opportunity.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I suppose it does make sense, if you put it like that. But, uhh, shouldn't you be prioritizing some more clear-cut issues? For example, Oren... Or is there something else you're worried about?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You're overthinking.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I carry out my duties in the manner I find logical.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Huh? The bell's ringing?

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: That's strange... The Abbot normally doesn't preach at this time, so why's the bell ringing right now?

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Oh, Clément! Talk about great timing! Do you know what's going on?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The abbot rang the bell because he decided last-minute to deliver a sermon today.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Let's head over to the chapel.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: That's... We should go, but we haven't finished our work yet.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Why the sudden sermon though? Does it have to do with the Laterans? Are they trying to... Uhh, are they here to cause trouble?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Why would you ask that?

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: It's not a big deal, just tell me if it's true or not... Hey, tell me, are they not letting us go to Laterano because Gerald's people are here?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Where'd you get that idea?

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: It's been on everyone's mind. The Sankta and the Sarkaz are on bad terms, right? If not for that fact, we might already be back in Laterano.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Well, there's no point talking about any of that now. I just don't know how the abbot feels about all this.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Clément, just forget I ever said anything. Nobody's blaming anyone, and there's nobody to blame in the first place. It's just that... the winter's not easy. The cold's awful.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Yes, I understand.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Everyone's just thinking, if we could go to Laterano, we'd have food, clothing, and work, right?

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: It'd be nice if there were some forests nearby. At least we'd be able to forage some branches to start a fire, so the kids could stay warm during the winter.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Yes, you're right... At least the kids would stay warm.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: But, would our lives really improve after we got to Laterano?

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Probably? I mean, where else would we go?

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: You don't need to worry yourself over that too much, Clément... God will protect us.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: What was that sound? What's going on this time...?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: (That sound...)

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: (...a gunshot?!)

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Clément has rung the bell...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Now, I should prepare my final...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Who's there?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Fortuna, my child, is that you?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Punctual as ever... Please take a seat until the others arrive.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I still need to finish a few things...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Fortuna?!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: What's the meaning of this...?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Avus... Stefano...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Help me...
The bloodstained girl stumbles toward the stunned old man, one step at a time.
The dim light finally illuminates the girl's face, revealing spotty traces of blood, as well as the black horns protruding from her forehead.
In front of her stands a statue of a gun-toting saint bathed in light, but behind her lies a trail of blood that cannot be erased.
Sankta blood drips onto the chapel's floorboards, giving off a dull sound. It is a deafening sound, one that opens all eyes wide.
The patron firearm used for prayer finally slips from the hands that were clutching it tightly.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina... Fina, she...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Don't cry, sweet child. What happened to Delfina?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: She's hurt!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: It was me. I hurt her... Avus Stefano, please save her!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Father! Are you alright? What happened–

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Fortuna...? What are you doing here? Is that... blood all over you...?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: What happened here?!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Huh? That's...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Woah, woah, woah. Is this for real?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: This ain't funny anymore.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: You people again... What the hell is going on here?!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Why has Fortuna grown a pair of black horns?!
The executor steps into the chapel under the watchful eyes of others.
The fallen angel continues to weep, but Stefano has no choice but to turn his eyes to the visitor.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The response from her halo is showing fluctuations, and horns are growing from her head. This is a clear indication that she has fallen.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: She has broken the Commandments.
